name: Sobia (Egyptian Chilled Coconut Drink)

ingredients.name: confectioners’ sugar, plus more as needed
ice cubes, plus more for serving

instructions.primary_message: For the Sobia Dry Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together coconut powder, milk powder, confectioners’ sugar, cream powder, vanilla powder, and salt. Transfer to an airtight container and store in a cool, dry place until ready to use.

To Make the Full Batch of Sobia: In a blender, combine milk, sobia dry mix, and ice. Blend until smooth, creamy, and frothy, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired. Pour into tall glasses filled with additional ice and serve immediately.
To Make One Serving of Sobia: In a blender, combine 2 1/2 to 3 tablespoons of the dry mix with 1 cup cold milk, and about 3 ice cubes, and blend until smooth, creamy, and frothy, about 1 minute. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired. Pour into a tall glass filled with additional ice and serve immediately.

description: This creamy Egyptian sobia blends coconut, milk, and vanilla into a frothy, ice-cold drink, with a make-ahead dry mix for easy serving.
notes:
Optional substitutions: unsweetened coconut milk powder → homemade coconut meal; whole milk → coconut milk or oat milk or almond milk

Notes: Coconut milk powder is available online and in some mainstream grocery stores. Alternatively, this recipe works well with homemade coconut meal. To make coconut meal at home, add 2 cups unsweetened shredded coconut to a high-powered blender and process until very finely ground, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed. Take care not to overprocess, or the coconut may begin to release its oils and turn pasty. This will yield about 1 cup coconut meal.
Heavy cream powder is dehydrated heavy cream that adds richness and body to the sobia without introducing additional liquid; it is widely available online.
Vanilla powder is typically made by combining vanilla extract or flavoring with a dry carrier such as maltodextrin, allowing it to be used in powdered form without adding liquid, which makes it especially useful in dry mixes like this one. It is widely available online; look for vanilla powder rather than vanilla-flavored sugar.

Make-ahead and storage: The sobia dry mix can be made up to 1 month in advance and stored in an airtight container in a cool, dark place.
author: Nermine Mansour
